solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Vampire seen in castle toured by Prince's second wife

indicators.note: to be toured by someone is to have them go all round you, so the castle sits inside the wife's name

parts.note: Camilla was the second wife of Prince Charles
R is the chess abbreviation for rook, also called a castle

explanation.surface: A royal visit: the Prince's second wife tours a castle and a vampire is spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: Camilla married Prince Charles (now King) in 2005; in chess notation R stands for the rook, which many players call a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmilla is the female vampire of Sheridan Le Fanu's 1872 novella, an early classic of vampire fiction.

clue.text: Rock star has head turned by ego, ultimately

indicators.note: turned means the slang word for head is read backwards

parts.note: nob is slang for the head

indicators.note: ultimately picks out the final letter of the word ego

explanation.surface: A swaggering rock star whose head has been turned by his own ego.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses NOB, and 'ultimately' takes the last letter of 'ego'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bono is the stage name of the lead singer of the Irish rock band U2.

clue.text: Number one daughter is into Wilde, surprisingly

indicators.note: the daughter's letter is into, that is placed inside, the rearranged surname
surprisingly signals that the letters of the writer's surname come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A dutiful daughter, the family's number one, is surprisingly a fan of Oscar Wilde.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' looks like praise; in British nursery talk it is a child's word for urinating. 'surprisingly' scrambles WILDE and 'is into' puts D inside.
explanation.definitionFit: In British childish euphemism 'number one' means urinating, and a widdle is the same thing in nursery language.

clue.text: Note the writer's point, perhaps writing to bully

parts.note: do is the first note of the tonic sol-fa scale
the writer's means belonging to me, the setter
a compass point, here E for east
R is one of the three Rs: reading, writing and arithmetic

explanation.surface: A schoolroom scene: a note, a point of view and some writing aimed at a bully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the writer's' is the setter speaking of himself, giving MINE; 'writing' gives R from the three Rs (reading, writing, arithmetic).
explanation.definitionFit: To domineer is to dominate others arrogantly, which is what a bully does, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Oddly GIs eat lemons regularly, without one getting the pips?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the scrambled letters go round the one
oddly signals that the letters are put together in a strange order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of lemons, starting with the first

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: American soldiers oddly eating lemons regularly, lacking one thing: the pips, like seeds of a fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking. The pips are not lemon seeds but the BBC's six radio beeps marking the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: The pips are the six short beeps broadcast on BBC radio to mark the exact hour, a well-known British time signal.

clue.text: Setter beset by Grandma's unwholesome atmosphere

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the setter's letter goes inside

parts.note: a grandma is one's ma's ma, mother's mother
the setter refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: A crossword setter visiting Grandma's house, surrounded by a stuffy, unwholesome atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: Grandma is rendered as MA'S MA (mother's mother), and the setter is I.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasma is a noxious or unhealthy vapour, historically blamed for disease, hence an unwholesome atmosphere.

clue.text: A head of Joyce, eighth element in false claim for pottery

indicators.note: in says the gathered letters are placed inside the rearranged word
false signals that the letters of claim are not in their true order
head of picks out the first letter of Joyce

parts.note: oxygen is element number eight, with symbol O

explanation.surface: A literary claim about James Joyce's head and some chemical element turns out to be false.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eighth element' is oxygen, number eight in the periodic table; its symbol joins A and Joyce's initial inside the scrambled claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Majolica is a tin-glazed earthenware, originally Italian Renaissance ware, so a kind of decorated pottery.

clue.text: Surprise attack by American president

parts.note: Bush is the surname of two US presidents

explanation.surface: A surprise attack launched by an American president.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambush is an attack sprung from hiding on an unsuspecting enemy, the classic surprise assault.

clue.text: Derivation of gold nib's core to first writings of Goldsmith, Irish novelist

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: core picks out the central letter of nib
first writings of takes the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Tracing the derivation of a gold pen nib back to the first writings of Oliver Goldsmith, the Irish novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is gold in heraldry; 'core' takes I from NIB, and 'first writings of' gives GIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A derivation is the source something comes from, which is what an origin is, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Gambon's place for Bible readings

indicators.note: the 's stands for has, so Gambon has the letters held inside his name

explanation.surface: The actor Michael Gambon's spot in church for reading the lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gambon's' reads as possessive, but it means 'Gambon has': the answer sits inside the name.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambo is a raised pulpit or reading desk in early churches, from which the scriptures were read.

clue.text: Sort of reggae cruise ships possibly book

parts.note: dub is a reggae style built on remixed instrumentals
cruise ships are an example of ocean liners

explanation.surface: A holiday picture: reggae music playing on cruise ships, with a book to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book' is the whole definition: Joyce's 1914 short-story collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubliners is James Joyce's 1914 collection of short stories, a celebrated book of Irish literature.

clue.text: Light up part of back lounge (Mulligan's)

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Lighting up a smoke in the back lounge of Mulligan's, a Dublin pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like part of 'back lounge' but reverses the letters hidden across 'lounge (Mulligan's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Illume is a poetic, archaic verb meaning to illuminate, that is to light up or brighten.

clue.text: Mischievously left "ass" in clue for 14 21's relative

definitions.note: the clue numbers name the Irish novelist from two other answers, whose 1864 novel title is a family member

indicators.note: mischievously signals that the letters are played about with

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone mischievously leaving the word 'ass' in a clue for an Irish writer's relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mischievously' scrambles L (left) with ASS IN CLUE. 14 and 21 together name the novelist Sheridan Le Fanu.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Silas is the 1864 gothic novel by Sheridan Le Fanu, whose title character is the heroine's uncle and guardian.

clue.text: Writer of Danish plays about a king or queen

indicators.note: about means round, so the scrambled letters go round the royal letters
plays means the letters of Danish move about freely

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina or Edward Rex, a queen or a king

explanation.surface: A writer of Danish plays about a royal figure, like Hamlet, Prince of Denmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays' is a verb, the anagram signal for DANISH. ER can be a queen (Elizabeth Regina) or a king (Edward Rex).
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Brinsley Sheridan was the Irish playwright of The Rivals and The School for Scandal, a celebrated writer.

clue.text: What could be read by checkout operator initially?

definitions.text: What could be read by checkout operator initially?

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters may be rearranged into something else
initially takes the first letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A question about what a supermarket cashier reads first on each item.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: 'could be' rearranges READ with B, C and O, the first letters of 'by checkout operator'.
explanation.definitionFit: Checkout operators scan the printed stripes on each item to identify it and its price, the first thing they read.

clue.text: Final resting place in end plot

parts.note: death is the end of life
a plot of ground in a garden is a bed

explanation.surface: A grave in a cemetery plot, someone's final resting place at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Final resting place' suggests a grave, but here it is the bed a person dies in.
explanation.definitionFit: A deathbed is the bed someone lies in as they die, cryptically the last place they rest.

clue.text: Three in one college

definitions.meaning: the Christian Godhead of Father, Son and Holy Spirit as three persons in one
the name of colleges at Cambridge, Oxford and Dublin

explanation.surface: Three people sharing one college room.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy Trinity is three persons in one God, and Trinity College is Dublin's ancient university.

clue.text: Body parts depicted by artist after outrageously hot, rampant sex

indicators.note: after places the artist's letters behind the scrambled hot
outrageously signals the letters of hot are thrown into disorder

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: rampant signals the letters of sex run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A racy painting: body parts depicted by an artist after hot, rampant sex.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a member of the Royal Academy, is the usual crossword artist; 'depicted by' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoraxes are chests, the parts of the body between neck and abdomen, so they are body parts.

clue.text: He mounted mule, having caught one to follow horse

indicators.note: to follow puts the remaining letters after the horse

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

indicators.note: having caught means the reversed word encloses the one
in a down clue mounted means the word goes upwards, read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A man climbs onto a mule, catching one to follow a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' looks like a pronoun but is the chemical symbol. 'mounted' turns MULE to ELUM, which catches I; H for horse (slang for heroin) comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the chemical symbol for the light, inert gas element number two.

clue.text: Turn off main road around lake, before a teen is sick

indicators.note: before puts the road and lake ahead of the scrambled teen
the main road goes around the lake's letter

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, with the 1 read as the letter I

indicators.note: is sick signals the letters of a teen are disordered

explanation.surface: A driver turns off the main road around a lake because a teenage passenger is sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn off' looks like a driving instruction but means to repel. 'is sick' rearranges A TEEN to ENATE. The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn someone off is to repel or estrange them, which is what alienating them does.

clue.text: In sauna, felt up writer

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the hidden letters are read from bottom to top
in says the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A cheeky scene in a sauna in which someone is groped, with a writer involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'felt up' reads as groping, but 'up' reverses the letters hidden in 'sauna, felt'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheridan Le Fanu was a nineteenth-century Irish novelist and ghost-story writer.

clue.text: Castrate old fart, primarily a musician

parts.note: to geld an animal is to castrate it

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: An instruction to castrate an old fart, who is primarily a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old fart' looks like a description of the musician, but only its first letters count.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Geldof is the Irish singer of the Boomtown Rats who organised Live Aid, a musician and campaigner.

clue.text: Sort of reggae briefly incorporating a type of dance music?

indicators.note: incorporating means the shuffled letters take in the a
sort of signals a rearranged version of the shortened word
briefly means the word is cut short by its final letter

explanation.surface: Asking whether a sort of reggae, cut short and blended with something, is a type of dance music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the last E of REGGAE; 'Sort of' rearranges REGGA, and 'incorporating' takes in A.
explanation.definitionFit: UK garage is a style of electronic dance music that grew out of 1990s house, named after a New York club.

clue.text: Worried if the girl becomes more giddy

indicators.note: worried signals that the letters are troubled into a new order

explanation.surface: If the girl becomes worried, she grows more giddy and anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Flighty means frivolous and fickle, so the comparative describes someone more giddy and capricious.

clue.text: GB sticker hated across Welsh borders

indicators.note: borders are edges, here the leading edge, the opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A GB car sticker is hated across the Welsh borders, where national pride runs high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'GB' reads as Great Britain, but here it is the initials of George Bernard Shaw.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright, is commonly known by his initials GBS.

clue.text: Dramatist uttered squeal

indicators.note: uttered means the playwright's name is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: J. M. Synge was the Irish dramatist of The Playboy of the Western World

explanation.surface: A playwright let out a squeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squeal' is not a noise here: it is slang for informing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To squeal on accomplices is criminal slang for informing to the police, also called to grass.

clue.text: 21's false leg's beginning to go hairy?

indicators.note: false signals that the remaining letters are not in their proper order
to go means the letter is taken away

parts.note: the Irish writer at 21 down, with the S of the possessive kept

indicators.note: beginning picks the first letter of leg

explanation.surface: An Irish writer's false leg, its beginning going hairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go' removes L (leg's beginning) from LEFANUS, and 'false' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairy is informal for frightening or dangerous, so a hairy situation is risky and insecure.

clue.text: Me cycling topless upset driver, of course

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over into a new order
topless means the word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: I was cycling topless and upset a driver, of course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' looks like a motorist, but is a golfer on a golf course. 'topless' drops C from CYCLING, and 'upset' rearranges ME with YCLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul McGinley is an Irish golfer and Ryder Cup captain, someone who drives off on a golf course.
